page.layout: One printed page: running head "NOTÆ." with page number 317 at top right. Main text in one column on the left, with Arabic script and Latin mixed. Marginal notes in the right margin, three of them, beside lines 2, 4 and 6 of the paragraph.; One column of Latin text with embedded Arabic lines, and a narrow column of marginal notes at the right, beside the lower half of the text. Below the text a rule runs across the page.

main_text.l: mus, alii dicunt, Mos est, &c.
Diei Veneris, &c. Dies iste appellationem يوم
الجمعة Taumol'Jomaa, Sortitus est الناس
لاجتماع quòd in eo congregentur homines [scil.ad cultus sa-
cros peragendos:] Magnis diem istum laudibus ef-
ferunt, سيد الايام Principem dierum vocantes. Sci-
endum autem (inquit AlGazalius) ان هذا اليوم فضل الله به
الاسلام وخص به المسلمين Deum huc di-
em velut honoris praerogativam Islamismo concessisse, eumque
Moslemis [seu Mohammedistis] proprium fecisse وجعله عيدا لهم فهم
اول الناس بها سبقا & illum, festum ipsis constituisse, atque ipsos primos eum
observasse. Et خير يوم طلعت عليه
الشمس يوم الجمعة Praestantissimum dierum quos superoritur sol, esse
diem Veneris. Eo futurum diem judicii autumant, &
ut videamus quibus tricis implicetur ipsorum reli-
gio, inter cætera quæ de eo nugantur, diem esse تقليم
الاظفار praescindis unguibus, præmii à Deo expe-
ctandi promisso, commendatum. من قلم
اظفاره Qui dies Veneris ungues praeciderit, eum Deus morbo libera-
tum sanitati restituit. Nuncupabatur olim عروبة A-
rubah, quod ait Al Jauharius esse من
اسمائهم nominibus eorum antiquis. Ita & Ahmed Iose-
phi filius كانت العرب تقول ليوم السبت شيار وليوم

page.notes: Arabic words in the main text and notes are transcribed from the scan and marked [?] where the letters are doubtful. The Arabic in the right margin notes is partly unclear. "Moslemis" is printed as shown. Arabic words and the Arabic marginal word are transcribed as far as legible; the exact Arabic spelling of several embedded words is uncertain.
